description: Hi I’m Biruk, a Grade 11 Natural Science student & web developer (HTML/CSS/JS) passionate about space tech and physics. For the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, I'm building a playable browser simulation game on managing life support and space hazards. Open to 100% remote teammates—join us for an organized, async-friendly build! Seeking skills in UI/Graphic Design, NASA/Space Research, Scenario Writing, or Video Pitching.
summary:
Mars Base Alpha is a browser-based 2D RPG resource management game created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer).

Students take control of a multi-wing base on Mars. Using the Radar Minimap, players move around the scrolling tile based station whilst managing three key resources; Power, Life Support & Radiation Shielding. Once a room has failed due to randomised emergencies or space weather events such as solar flares or dust storms, the player must engage with interactive engineering puzzles including aligning circuits, balancing pressure and filling bladders in water walls.

The game addresses the challenge by using real data from NASA. The NASA DONKI Space Weather API provides the real time data, with a backup option for the Curiosity RAD surface radiation data. Students learn about real trade-offs in space exploration. You can see that any fixes to the systems require a balance of resources.

This project is important because it takes complicated aerospace engineering concepts and makes them easy to access and fun! It encourages the next generation of scientists and engineers by getting them involved in solving problems.
details:
The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an engaging 2D browser based Role Playing Game (RPG) aimed at children aged 7-12. It involves playing as a junior astronaut on Mars. The goal is to manage your resources; power, Life Support and Radiation Shielding. The game includes a large scrollable tile-based world, with realistic wall collisions, and a live radar mini map. During the game you’ll have to manage unexpected events such as pressure leaks, solar flares and solar panel issues. These will make your screen go into emergency mode and you’ll have to solve problems using mini games to keep the spacecraft running; such as aligning circuits and balancing pressures.

This project has great accessibility and educational benefits. As it is a browser based game there is no downloading, installing or logging in – making it easy for children, teachers and judges to play. Complex aerospace engineering ideas and resource management have been turned into simple, fun game mechanics. This will help encourage young minds to become interested in space exploration, planetary science and engineering. Especially with young people from less well off areas. It also teaches children to think critically and quickly.

The game was developed using a purely web based tech stack. Using only HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript. It uses HTML5 Canvas to create a 2D game. It uses the live NASA DONKI Space Weather API to provide alerts for solar flares and protons. If there are no alerts it will fall back to the NASA Curiosity RAD data. The code was created using Visual Studio Code and using Git. The code can be found on GitHub Pages.

The creativity of the game comes from using real time data. The game does not use completely fictional hazards but instead real space weather. The game does not use simple click buttons but instead provides hands on engineering challenges. The game also has a sleek high tech HUD and retro look to keep children engaged. Accessibility was kept in mind when creating the game. Puzzles have been made to be challenging enough for the age group (7-12). The game also has good back up options to work offline.
